identity_provider.preset.google.particul: One issuer serves every Google account there is, private ones included. Hubtask therefore never lets in everybody with a Google account: only people invited here, or people from the Google Workspace domains you list. A personal Google account belongs to no domain and comes in only by invitation.
identity_provider.preset.google.instruct: In the Google Cloud console, create an OAuth client of type "Web application" and add the redirect address below as an authorised redirect URI. Copy the client id and secret here.
identity_provider.preset.microsoft.parti: Register the application in your own directory. That directory's own issuer address serves that directory; a shared address serves every directory you list below, and nobody else.
identity_provider.preset.microsoft.instr: In Entra ID, register an application, add the redirect address below as a web redirect URI, and create a client secret. The issuer is the one your directory's OpenID configuration names.
identity_provider.preset.generic.instruc:
Register Hubtask as a confidential client that supports the authorization code flow with PKCE, and add the redirect address below as its redirect URI. Hubtask asks for the openid, email and profile scopes and reads the issuer's discovery document, so anything that publishes one works - Keycloak, Authentik, Okta, Zitadel, Auth0, GitLab, a directory of your own.

Where to look, by name: Keycloak calls it Clients, with Client authentication on and Standard flow enabled, and the issuer is your realm's address. Authentik calls it Providers, OAuth2/OpenID, Confidential. Okta calls it Applications, Web Application. Zitadel calls it Applications, Web, Code with PKCE. Auth0 calls it Applications, Regular Web Application.

Two things that are not obvious. The issuer is the address whose discovery document names itself - not the sign-in page, and usually not the address you registered at; paste it and Hubtask fetches it before saving, so a wrong one is refused here rather than by the first person who tries. And Hubtask cannot tell whether this provider verifies the addresses it hands out, so an account that already exists here is connected to it only after that account's own password. Invited people accept their invitation through this provider from their invitation's own link - choosing the provider on the sign-in page instead is refused, because Hubtask cannot tell whether this provider runs their mailbox.

lifecycle.legal_hold: {scope, select, WORKSPACE {A legal hold is in force in this workspace, so it cannot be deleted or reset to a backup until every hold is released.} TENANT {This cannot be deleted for good: a legal hold is in force on the whole workspace. Ask whoever placed it.} CONTAINER {This cannot be deleted for good: a legal hold is in force on the hub or collection it is in. Ask whoever placed it.} ITEM {This cannot be deleted for good: a legal hold is in force on this entry or one it sits under. Ask whoever placed it.} ACCOUNT {This cannot be deleted for good: a legal hold is in force on the data of a person who contributed to it. Ask whoever placed it.} other {This cannot be deleted for good: a legal hold is in force. Ask whoever placed it.}}
lifecycle.hold_incomplete: That legal hold cannot be placed as described.
lifecycle.hold_scope_invalid: A legal hold covers the workspace, a hub or collection, an entry, or a person.
lifecycle.hold_scope_id_mismatch: A hold on the whole workspace names nothing, and a hold on anything else has to name it.
lifecycle.hold_reason_required: A legal hold needs a reason, and so does lifting one - it is what somebody reading the record later has to go on.
lifecycle.hold_reason_too_long: That reason is longer than a legal hold can carry. Keep it to the substance and the citation.
lifecycle.hold_not_found: There is no such legal hold.
lifecycle.hold_target_not_found: This workspace has nothing by that identifier to hold.
lifecycle.hold_already_released: That legal hold has already been lifted.
lifecycle.hold_replaced: A legal hold was placed again after the installation was recovered to an earlier moment.
lifecycle.recovery_point_required: Name the moment the installation was recovered to.
lifecycle.holds_required: Send at least one legal hold to place again.
lifecycle.too_many_holds: At most {maximum} legal holds go in one call; send the rest in another.
lifecycle.holds_source_ambiguous: Send the legal holds or name an archive to read them from, not both.
lifecycle.hold_archive_incomplete: Name the backup target and the path of the archive to read the legal holds from.
lifecycle.hold_archive_not_wired: This installation is misconfigured: it cannot read the legal holds of an archive.
lifecycle.removal_incomplete: This installation is misconfigured and could not record that deletion.
lifecycle.removal_reasons_mixed: This installation is misconfigured and could not record that deletion.
lifecycle.policy_not_found: No retention period is configured for that kind of data.
lifecycle.run_unrecordable: This installation could not record what a deletion run did.
lifecycle.history_not_wired: This installation is misconfigured: nothing removes the notification history when its period runs out.
lifecycle.inbox_not_wired: This installation is misconfigured: nothing removes jumble entries when their period runs out.
lifecycle.rule_incomplete: That retention rule cannot be created as described.
lifecycle.data_kind_unknown: That is not a kind of data Hubtask keeps a period for.
lifecycle.data_kind_not_swept: Hubtask does not yet remove {data_kind}, so a period for it would be a promise nothing keeps. Ask for it in a later release rather than configuring one that never runs.
lifecycle.scope_invalid: A retention rule applies to the workspace, a hub or a collection.
lifecycle.scope_id_mismatch: A rule for the whole workspace names no hub or collection, and a rule for one has to name it.
lifecycle.action_invalid: That is not something a retention rule can do.
lifecycle.action_not_performed: Hubtask cannot {action} {data_kind} yet. Choose another action.
lifecycle.retain_days_invalid: A retention period cannot be a negative number of days.
lifecycle.condition_invalid: That condition is not a valid expression.
lifecycle.expression_engine_unavailable: This installation cannot check conditions, so it will not store or act on one.
lifecycle.chain_incomplete: A second stage needs both a period and an action.
lifecycle.chain_has_no_second_stage: There is nothing left to act on after {action}, so it cannot be followed by a second stage.
lifecycle.below_lower_bound: {data_kind} is kept for at least {min_days} days, so that a mistake in a rule cannot delete something the moment it appears.
lifecycle.justification_required: Keeping {data_kind} longer than {max_days} days needs a justification, and it is written into the audit trail.
lifecycle.grace_not_applicable: {data_kind} has no grace period of its own: it is announced by being where it is, and warning about it again would be warning twice.
lifecycle.grace_invalid: A grace period cannot be a negative number of days.
lifecycle.recipient_invalid: That is not somebody a retention rule can warn.
lifecycle.notify_beyond_grace: A warning has to arrive inside the grace period, which is {grace_days} days.
lifecycle.export_target_required: Exporting before deletion needs a backup target to write the archive to.
lifecycle.export_unavailable: This installation cannot write an export, so a rule that exports before deleting is not carried out - deleting without the export is not what the rule says.
lifecycle.rule_not_found: There is no such retention rule.
lifecycle.rule_already_exists: There is already a retention rule for that kind of data at that level.
lifecycle.rule_version_conflict: Somebody else changed that retention rule. Read it again and retry.
lifecycle.not_marked: That entry is not in a retention period, so there is nothing to take it out of.
lifecycle.rule_changed: A retention rule was created or changed.
lifecycle.retained: An entry was taken out of its retention period.
lifecycle.restriction: This cannot be deleted: processing of it is restricted while a data subject request is open.
lifecycle.descendant_retained: This cannot be deleted yet: something below it is kept for longer.

email.password_reset.subject: Reset your Hubtask password
email.password_reset.body:
Somebody asked to reset the password for this address. Choose a new one here: {link}

The link works once and for thirty minutes. If it was not you, you can ignore this message - nothing has changed.
email.password_reset_provider.subject: About your Hubtask sign-in
email.password_reset_provider.body: Somebody asked for a way to sign in with this address. This account signs in through your organisation's provider, so there is no password here to reset and no link to send - sign in the way you usually do. If it was not you, you can ignore this message.
email.password_set.subject: Set a password for Hubtask
email.password_set.body:
Somebody asked to reset the password for this address. This account signed in through a provider your workspace no longer has, so for now you sign in with a password instead. Choose one here: {link}

The link works once and for thirty minutes. If it was not you, you can ignore this message - nothing has changed.
email.password_connect.subject: Connect your Hubtask sign-in
email.password_connect.body:
Somebody asked for a sign-in link for this address. Your workspace no longer signs in with a password, and this account is not connected to its provider yet. Connect it here: {link}

The link works once and for thirty minutes. Sign in at the provider with this address; if the account has a second factor, it is asked for as usual. If it was not you, you can ignore this message - nothing has changed.
email.address_confirm.subject: Confirm your address for Hubtask
email.address_confirm.body:
Somebody asked to add this address to the Hubtask account of {name}. Confirm it here: {link}

The link works once and for a day. Once confirmed, the account signs in with this address too, and a forgotten password can be reset by mail. If you do not know about this, ignore this message - nothing changes.
email.password_opened.subject: The password is open for {workspace}
email.password_opened.body:
The operator of this installation opened the password for {workspace} until {until}. Until then everybody there who holds a password can sign in with it, whatever your sign-in settings say - usually because your provider cannot be reached. Who asked for it and why is in the workspace's audit trail. If nobody in your workspace asked for this, tell the operator.

{link}
email.password_closed.subject: The password is closed again for {workspace}
email.password_closed.body:
The operator's opening of the password for {workspace} has ended. Your own sign-in settings decide again.

{link}
email.password_closed_early.body:
The operator closed the password for {workspace} before the opening's time was up. Your own sign-in settings decide again.

{link}

automation.rule_unreadable: That rule was stored in a shape this version cannot read.
automation.rule_unserialisable: This installation could not store that rule.

app.signin_settings.title: Sign-in
app.signin_settings.lead: How people in this workspace prove who they are. What the installation has already decided is shown beside each rule, and a lock means it decided for every workspace.
app.signin_settings.managed_accounts: Accounts without a mail address allowed
app.signin_settings.managed_accounts_hin: Owners and administrators may give somebody an account with a sign-in name instead of an address. Switching this off stops new ones; the ones already here keep signing in.
app.signin_settings.managed_off_above: Switched off above this workspace, so it cannot be switched on here.
app.signin_settings.legal_hint: Shown in the footer of the sign-in screen. Leave one empty to use the installation's.
app.signin_settings.classes: At least this many of each kind
app.signin_settings.classes_hint: Length protects more than kinds do. A script without upper and lower case can never meet the first two.
app.signin_settings.min_classes: At least this many of the four kinds
app.signin_settings.max_repeat: Most of the same character in a row
app.signin_settings.context_words: Refuse the address, the name and the workspace name inside a password
app.signin_settings.breach_hint: Five characters of a hash leave this server. Off unless the installation allows it.
app.signin_settings.max_age_hint: Empty means it does not expire, which is what is recommended.
app.signin_settings.history_hint: 0 to 10. Each one costs a comparison when somebody sets a password.
app.signin_settings.min_age_hint: How long a new password stands before it may be changed again. 0 is at once; a reset is never held back.
app.signin_settings.adds_a_line: Adds a line to every password screen.
app.signin_settings.mfa_hint: Everybody it applies to sets one up at their next sign-in, including you.
app.signin_settings.mfa_everyone: Everyone signing in with a password
app.signin_settings.session_max_days: End a session after, in days
app.signin_settings.session_idle: End an idle session after, in minutes
app.signin_settings.session_idle_hint: Empty means an idle session is not ended.
app.signin_settings.locked_installation: Set by the installation for every workspace.
app.changes.title: History & versions
app.changes.intro: Every configuration change applied here, the changes proposed for a person to decide, and the configuration file the API, hubctl and agents read.
app.changes.none_proposed: Nothing is waiting for a decision.
app.changes.acknowledge: I have seen that this hides data or changes what people may do
app.changes.acknowledge_first: Confirm first that you have seen what this change does.
app.changes.no_versions: No change has been applied through the configuration document yet.

app.password.connect_intro: This workspace signs in through its provider, not with a password. Sign in there with the address this link was sent to, and the provider is connected to your account - from then on it signs you in. If your account has a second factor, it is asked next.
app.recovery.title: Recovery codes
app.recovery.none_left: None left. Make new ones before your authenticator is out of reach.
app.recovery.regenerate_hint: The ten you have now stop working the moment the new ones appear.
app.recovery.none_yet: Ten codes come with the second factor, and there is no second factor on this account yet. Set one up and they are shown once, at the end.
app.recovery.acknowledge: I have stored these codes. They will not be shown again.
app.recovery.not_acknowledged: Confirm you have stored them, then this can be closed.
app.callback.title: Signing you in
app.callback.working: Finishing the sign-in with your provider.
app.callback.step_up_working: Finishing the confirmation with your provider.
app.callback.connect_working: Finishing the connection with your provider.
app.admin.title: Administration
app.admin.trail: Where you are in the administration
app.admin_overview.title: Overview
app.admin_overview.limits_none: No limit with a ceiling counts anything here yet.
app.admin_overview.rules_none: No rule fails or needs a look.
app.admin_overview.backup_no_target: No backup target is set up, so nothing is backed up.
app.admin_overview.backup_none: No backup has been written yet.
app.admin_overview.requests_none: No request is owed in the next seven days.
app.admin.installation: Applies to every workspace you create
app.instance.trail: Where you are in the installation
app.instance.plans_intro: A plan groups workspaces with values, limits and features of its own, between the installation and the workspace. Hubtask ships none; a workspace without one has the installation's values and every feature.
app.instance.plans_single: Plans exist where an installation runs several workspaces; this one runs one.
app.instance.plans_without: Without a plan: {count, plural, one {# workspace} other {# workspaces}}. They have the installation's values and every feature.
app.instance.plan_short_name_hint: What the purchase platform maps its products to: 2 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It never changes and is never used again.
app.instance.plan_features_hint: A feature switched off rests in every workspace on the plan: nothing is deleted, and it works again from the moment it is switched on.
app.instance.plan_value_overtaken: The plan's own value, {value}, is not in force: the installation locks it, and a save that keeps it is refused.
app.instance.plan_falls_back: Not decided by the plan: the installation's applies, {value}.
app.instance.plan_falls_back_default: Not decided by the plan or the installation: Hubtask's default applies.
app.instance.plan_limits_exception: An operator's exception for one workspace stays the last word on a limit.
app.instance.plan_confirm_body: {count, plural, =0 {No workspace is on this plan yet.} one {It changes at once for the # workspace on this plan.} other {It changes at once for all # workspaces on this plan.}}
app.instance.plan_conflict_title: Somebody saved the plan in the meantime.
app.instance.plan_conflict_body: Read it again and carry your changes over; nothing was overwritten.
app.instance.plan_remove_body: No workspace is on it. Its short name {short} stays taken and is never used again.
app.instance.move_exceeded: {limits}. What exists stays; only something new is refused.
app.instance.move_nothing: Nothing rests, no limit is exceeded, and no exception stays.
app.instance.new_plan_hint: What the workspace starts on. It can be changed later under Change plan.
app.instance.locked_intro: These screens run the installation rather than this workspace: which workspaces exist, what applies to all of them, and who may change it. Reaching them needs you to prove who you are again.
app.instance.locked_cost: The proof lasts an hour, on this session only, and it does not extend itself. It is written into the installation's journal, as is the moment it ends.
app.instance.elevated: You are working on the installation. {clock} left.
app.instance.workspaces_intro: Every workspace on this installation, with its standing. What is inside one is not shown here and cannot be reached from here.
app.instance.workspaces_none: No workspace has been provisioned yet.
app.instance.workspaces_service_only: {count, plural, one {# more workspace holds only service accounts and is not counted.} other {# more workspaces hold only service accounts and are not counted.}}
app.instance.health_ok: Everything this installation depends on is answering.
app.instance.health_degraded: Something this installation depends on is not answering. What still works, works.
app.instance.purge_started: Being removed since {at}; the deletion can no longer be called off
app.instance.legal_hold_note: A legal hold is in force, so the workspace cannot be deleted until its owner releases every hold.
app.instance.legal_hold_waits: A legal hold is in force: the deletion waits until every hold is released. Its people cannot release one while the workspace is being deleted; cancel the deletion first.
app.instance.targets_intro: This installation's own backup targets: where a workspace that has no target of its own is exported to. No workspace sees them; the export offers them by name. Adding or removing one asks you to prove it is you again.
app.instance.targets_none: This installation has no backup target of its own yet.
app.instance.targets_add: Add a target of the installation
app.instance.targets_remove_note: The exports already written to {name} stay where they are; only this installation's way of reaching them goes.
app.instance.platform_redelivered_announ: The undeliverable events are being delivered again.
app.instance.platform_unreachable_title: The platform could not be reached.
app.instance.platform_unreachable_body: The subscription stays on; the undeliverable events are ready to be delivered again. The platform can also read the events it missed itself.
app.instance.platform_sent: Sent are: created, plan changed, suspended, active again, deletion requested, cancelled and done, owner changed, limit reached, AI budget spent, export finished. Only identifiers and states, never content.
app.instance.platform_none: No platform is subscribed. The events are kept for 30 days all the same, and can be read from the feed.
app.instance.platform_single: This installation runs one workspace, so there is no purchase platform to tell.
app.instance.platform_secret_hint: Give it to the platform now: it checks every event's signature with it, and it is not shown again.
app.instance.platform_target_hint: Every event is sent here as a signed CloudEvent.
app.instance.platform_remove_note: Nothing more is sent to {target}. The events stay readable from the feed.
app.instance.export_target_own: A target of the workspace itself
app.instance.export_target_id_hint: Its identifier, as the workspace's backup screen shows it.
app.instance.ai_intro: The AI models this installation offers every workspace. Offered is not on: each workspace chooses a model itself, and that choice is its consent to send its content there. A workspace sees each model's name, who processes it and where - never its address, its models or its key.
app.instance.ai_none: This installation offers no AI model. Each workspace connects its own, where the defaults allow it - or none.
app.instance.ai_unreachable_title: No workspace can choose these models yet
app.instance.ai_unreachable_body: "{setting}" in the defaults leaves the offered model out, so no workspace is shown it.
app.instance.ai_remove_cost: Every workspace that uses {name} gets no AI answer until it chooses again. Nothing a workspace configured itself is touched, and nothing anybody accepted is undone.
app.instance.ai_form_intro: Every workspace sees the name, the processor and where it processes content before it agrees. Changing the model for meaning makes each workspace using it rebuild its search by meaning in the background.
app.instance.ai_name_hint: What workspaces choose it by, unique among the models offered here.
app.instance.ai_processor_hint: Who processes what is sent to it, as you declare it.
app.instance.ai_operator_only: The address, the models and the key stay the installation's: no workspace sees them.
app.instance.suspend_cost: Its people can no longer work in it from their next step on, and are told it is paused. Nothing in it is lost, its export still works, and Resume brings it back as it was.
app.instance.suspend_own: This is your own workspace. Your session ends at once, and only an operator from another workspace can resume it.
app.instance.providers_intro: The ways in this installation offers every workspace on it. Offered is not on: each workspace's owner decides whether to take one - except where the installation's ways to sign in are locked with providers among them, which turns on every provider that admits only invited people. Each row says which applies.
app.instance.providers_none: This installation offers no provider of its own. Every workspace configures its own, or none.
app.instance.provider_lock_turns_on: On in every workspace: the ways to sign in are locked, and it admits only invited people.
app.instance.provider_lock_leaves_to_wor: Each workspace's own choice: the lock on the ways to sign in turns on only providers that admit invited people alone.
app.instance.provider_lock_would_turn_on: Locking the ways to sign in with providers among them turns it on in every workspace.
app.instance.provider_withdraw_intro: Until the day you choose it keeps working, and every workspace that uses it tells its administrators on their sign-in settings when it ends. You can keep offering it at any time, after the day too: nobody's connection to it is removed.
app.instance.provider_withdraw_date_hint: It ends when that day begins. Two weeks give every workspace that uses it time to switch on another way.
app.instance.provider_withdraw_now_intro: For a provider that is compromised. It ends at once in every workspace, and a workspace left with no other way falls back to the password for the accounts that hold one. To confirm, type how many workspaces use it.
app.instance.provider_form_intro: Hubtask fetches the issuer's metadata before storing anything, so an address that cannot be reached is refused here rather than by the first person who tries to sign in.
app.instance.provider_position_hint: The order the buttons are drawn in, lowest first.
app.instance.provider_remove_cost: Removing deletes the provider and every connection between a person and it; offering it again does not restore them. The accounts keep their work and the session they are in right now; a workspace left with no other way falls back to the password for the accounts that hold one.
app.instance.provider_remove_first: Withdraw it first: workspaces still use it.
app.instance.provider_remove_after: Its withdrawal is announced: it can be removed from {date}.
app.instance.provider_invited_only: Offered to every workspace, a provider without a directory lets in only the people each workspace invited. Anyone else it knows is turned away.
app.instance.encryption_intro: The keys this installation seals values under, and how many stored values still name each. Read here; turned at the terminal, because a rotation needs the new key in the environment and no screen can put it there.
app.instance.encryption_none: This installation seals nothing: no key is configured.
app.instance.encryption_rotation_title: Rotating is not done from here
app.instance.encryption_rotation: A new key goes into the environment first and the values are re-sealed by an operation run against the installation. A button here could start a rotation for a key no process is holding, which is how a ring ends up with values nothing can open.
app.instance.encryption_stranded_title: A key is missing and values still name it
app.instance.encryption_stranded: Nothing can open what {keys} sealed until the key is back in the ring. Every read of those values answers a refusal until then.
app.instance.encryption_stranded_kind: Still sealed under {key}: {count, plural, one {# {store, select, account_mfa {second factor} identity_provider {sign-in provider secret} webhook_subscription {webhook signing secret} backup_target {backup target credential} ai_provider {AI provider key} automation_rule {rule header secret} automation_http_job {header secret of a pending HTTP call} backup_archive {backup archive} cmdb_connector {CMDB connector credential} other {stored secret}}} other {# {store, select, account_mfa {second factors} identity_provider {sign-in provider secrets} webhook_subscription {webhook signing secrets} backup_target {backup target credentials} ai_provider {AI provider keys} automation_rule {rule header secrets} automation_http_job {header secrets of pending HTTP calls} backup_archive {backup archives} cmdb_connector {CMDB connector credentials} other {stored secrets}}}}.
app.instance.workspace_new_intro: A workspace, and the person who owns it. Nobody else is added: the owner invites whoever belongs there, and this installation never sees what they put inside.
app.instance.slug_hint: Lower case letters, digits and hyphens. It appears in addresses and cannot be changed afterwards.
app.instance.owner_email_hint: They receive nothing from here. Hand them the token this screen shows once the workspace exists.
app.instance.owner_token_hint: It is shown this once and is not stored anywhere it can be read again. The owner exchanges it for their own password.
app.instance.owner_token_keep_first: Confirm that you have it before closing this, because nothing can show it a second time.
app.instance.delete_cost: The workspace stops answering at once and everything in it is removed for good when the grace period ends. Until then it can be called off, and after it nothing can.
app.instance.delete_confirm_hint: Exactly as it is written above.
app.instance.delete_own: This is your own workspace. Your session ends at once, and only an operator from another workspace can cancel the deletion.
app.instance.password_open_cost: For a sign-in provider that is switched on but broken. Everybody in this workspace who holds a password can sign in with it until the time is up, whatever the workspace's own settings say, and its administrators are told when it opens and when it closes. Nothing in the workspace is read or changed.
app.instance.password_open_hours_hint: From now: one to {maximum}. A day unless you say otherwise.
app.instance.password_open_requester_hin: A ticket reference rather than a name, where you have one. The workspace's administrators read it.
app.instance.password_open_reason_hint: What is wrong with the provider. Recorded with the opening in the workspace's trail and in this installation's journal.
app.instance.export_intro: Everything the workspace holds, as one documented archive written to a target. The archive is not encrypted - it is the workspace's way out - and the export is recorded in the workspace's trail.
app.instance.export_target_hint: One of this installation's targets, or one of the workspace's own.
app.instance.quotas_intro: What this workspace may use. An empty field means the value without an exception - the plan's or this installation's - rather than none.
app.instance.quota_default: Empty uses this installation's own ceiling: {value}.
app.instance.quota_plan_default: Empty uses the limit of the plan {plan}: {value}.
app.instance.quota_product_default: This installation has set no ceiling here, so empty uses Hubtask's own.
app.instance.quota.ai_arrival_proposals_: Jumble entries AI reads on arrival per day
app.instance.operators_intro: An operator can reach these screens after proving who they are. Anyone else is refused, whatever else they may do in their own workspace.
app.instance.operators_empty: Nobody is registered, which on a private installation means the owner - exactly as it did before this register existed. Adding the first operator turns that off.
app.instance.operator_account_hint: The account's identifier. Their workspace comes from the account itself, so there is nothing else to fill in.
app.instance.operator_workspace_hint: The workspace the account lives in. A person in two workspaces has two accounts, so this says which one.
app.instance.operator_email_hint: The address they sign in with. Hubtask looks up the account itself - there is no identifier to find, because no screen may list accounts across workspaces.
app.instance.operator_service_account: A service account - it signs in nowhere
app.instance.operator_last_note: The only operator cannot be removed: an installation nobody operates is one nobody can run.
app.instance.operator_first_note: Nobody is registered yet, so you work on the installation as the owner of its only workspace. Adding somebody adds you as well, so that you keep it.
app.instance.operator_service_title: Make a service account an operator
app.instance.operator_service_intro: The service accounts of the workspace you are signed in to. A platform that creates workspaces uses one, so that it keeps working when the person who set it up leaves.
app.instance.operator_service_none: This workspace has no service account that is not an operator already. Create one under Administration, Service accounts.
app.instance.operator_remove_body: {name} of {workspace} will no longer reach the installation's screens. Their account stays as it is.
app.instance.operator_remove_self_body: You will no longer reach the installation's screens. Your account in your workspace stays as it is.
app.instance.operator_remove_self_again_: The installation closes to you at once
The moment you confirm, these screens are closed to you, and only another operator can add you again.
app.instance.settings_intro: What this installation has decided for every workspace on it. Changed here, through hubctl, or through the API - they are three doors to the same values. A file in enforcing mode is the exception: then it is the source and nothing else may write.
app.instance.settings_none: This installation has decided nothing of its own, so every workspace decides for itself.
app.instance.settings_edit_hint: A setting left on "Each workspace decides" is one this installation does not decide. Beside each value: what a workspace may still do with it.
app.instance.settings_saved: Saved. Every workspace reads the new values from now on.
app.instance.presets_about: Offered to every workspace when somebody creates a hub or collection, marked as the installation's. Hubs and collections made from one keep their settings when it is renamed, changed or withdrawn.
app.instance.presets_none: No presets of the installation yet. Every workspace is offered Hubtask's and its own.
app.instance.presets_is_default: New workspaces start from this preset.
app.instance.presets_withdraw_default: New workspaces start from this preset. Choose another default, or none, first.
app.instance.presets_default_hint: Used for a new hub where its workspace chose no default of its own. Choosing one changes no workspace that exists.
app.instance.presets_locks_hint: A locked setting keeps the default preset's value in every workspace, hub and collection; no workspace can change it.
app.instance.presets_field_locks: {count, plural, one {One field of a level is locked as well.} other {# fields of levels are locked as well.}}
app.instance.presets_field_locks_short: {count, plural, one {one field of a level} other {# fields of levels}}
app.instance.presets_created: Preset created. Every workspace offers it now.
app.instance.presets_withdrawn: Preset withdrawn. No workspace offers it any more.
app.instance.locked_never_localisation: A language, a time zone or a week start is a suggestion. A workspace that could not choose its own would be a product defect.
app.instance.locked_with_terms_link: The version is locked together with the terms link.
app.instance.blocklist_hint: A file on this installation, one password per line. Leave it empty to refuse none.
app.instance.settings_decided: This installation has decided {decided} of {total} settings. The rest are each workspace's.
app.instance.setting.sign_in.min_classes: At least this many of the four kinds
app.instance.setting.sign_in.max_repeat: Most of the same character in a row
app.instance.setting.sign_in.context_wor: Refuse the address, the name and the workspace name inside a password
app.instance.setting.sign_in.session_max: End a session after, in days
app.instance.setting.sign_in.session_idl: End an idle session after, in minutes
app.instance.setting.sign_in.managed_acc: Accounts without a mail address allowed
app.instance.setting.ai.min_jurisdiction: Their own model must process content
app.instance.setting.ai.person_opt_out: Each person may keep their own content out of AI
app.instance.setting.sign_in.mfa_require: A second factor is required of
app.instance.setting.quotas.api_requests: Requests through the API per minute
app.instance.setting.quotas.ai_arrival_p: Jumble entries AI reads on arrival per day
app.instance.choice.sign_in.mfa_required: Everyone signing in with a password
app.instance.choice.ai.sources.EITHER: The offered model or their own
In the EEA or a country with an adequacy decision
app.instance.choice.ai.person_opt_out.OF: Yes - only a workspace can make AI part of everybody's work
app.instance.lock_needs_value: Choose a value first: a setting this installation does not decide has nothing to hold workspaces to.
app.instance.source_database: These values were set through the API and are stored in the database.
app.instance.source_file: These values come from this installation's file and were written at start.
app.instance.source_file_enforced: These values come from this installation's file and are written again at every start. Changing them here or through the API is refused.
app.instance.journal_intro: What this installation recorded: who was provisioned, suspended, resumed and deleted, and what its operator changed. Identifiers, counts and moments - never anybody's content, which is what makes it readable after the workspace it names is gone.
app.instance.journal_intro_single: What was recorded here about every workspace you create: what was set up, which defaults and locks changed, who may change them, and who did. Identifiers, counts and moments - never anybody's content.
app.instance.journal_workspace_hint: Also of a workspace that is gone.
app.instance.journal_arrived: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing more arrived.} one {# more entry arrived.} other {# more entries arrived.}}
app.instance.digest_settings: {decided} of {total} settings decided, {locked} of them locked
app.instance.digest_legal_state: {decided} of {total} links set, {locked} of them locked
app.instance.digest_providers_none: This installation offers none of its own
app.instance.digest_operators: {count, plural, one {# account may run this installation} other {# accounts may run this installation}}
app.instance.digest_operators_sole: You run this installation because it has one workspace and nobody is registered.
app.instance.later_retention: Default retention rules with a lock, and how long the audit trail is kept.
app.instance.action.instance_backup_targ: Backup target of the installation configured

Backup target of the installation tested
app.instance.action.instance_secrets_res: Installation secrets re-sealed under the current key
app.instance.action.tenant_reference_cha: Platform reference of a workspace changed
app.agents.title: Agents
app.agents.intro: Agents act for a person and never do what that person may not. Nothing an agent attempts runs until somebody other than that person approved it and put it live.
app.agents.none: No agent is registered here yet.
app.agents.change_hint: A change that lets the agent do more - wider scopes, another model, a looser rule, a lower bar, another owner - takes it back to a draft until it is approved again.
app.agents.name: Name
app.agents.purpose_hint: The trail records the agent without its purpose.
app.agents.owner_hint: The person it acts for; it never does what they may not, and they do not approve it.
app.agents.risk_hint: An agent that would decide about people is not registered at all.
app.agents.scopes_hint: Separated by spaces or commas, for example items:read items:write.
app.agents.reversible: An act that can be taken back
app.agents.irreversible: An act that cannot be taken back
app.agents.min_accuracy_hint: Above 0, the agent goes live only once a run of its evaluation set on its model reached this.
agents.registration_required: This workspace takes registered agents only on MCP. Ask an administrator to register this agent.
app.agents.registered_only_hint: A person's own token or a service account no agent names is refused on MCP.
app.agents.registered_only_locked: The installation or the plan switched this on and locked it.
app.agents.halted_title: Every agent of this workspace is halted
app.agents.halted_since: Halted by {name}, {at}. Every act any agent attempts is refused until the agents are released.
app.agents.ledger_empty: The agent has attempted nothing yet.
app.agents.runs_when_live: A job runs once the agent is live.
app.agents.target_entry: The entry the agent works on:
app.agents.target_hub: The hub whose inventory it reviews
app.agents.target_needed: Choose what the agent works on.
app.agents.job_started: The job started; what it proposes waits for a person.
app.agents.bar: It goes live once a run on its model reached {min_accuracy} %.
app.agents.no_bar: It asks for no evaluation before going live.
app.agents.cases_empty: The set holds no case yet.
app.agents.case_expected_hint: As JSON: each key is compared, a list as a set.
app.agents.expected_not_json: The expected answer is not JSON.
app.agents.expected_not_object: The expected answer is an object of keys.
app.agents.runs_empty: The agent has not answered its set yet.
app.agents.evaluated: The agent answered its set; the run is recorded.
app.agents.evaluation_hub_needed: Choose the hub whose CIs it matches.
app.agents.request_approved: Done, as you and with your rights.
app.agents.models_intro: The models agents may call. Registering one is the consent to send agents' material to it.
app.agents.models_empty: No model is registered for agents yet.
app.agents.model_consent: Saving is your consent to send agents' material to this model. A change of what it is asks every agent using it for approval again.
app.agents.model_key_hint: Lower-case letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.
app.agents.model_needs_name: Give the model a name and say which model it is.
app.agents.retention_hint: Days the provider keeps what it is sent; empty is not known.
app.agents.retire_model: Retired: every agent using it stops
app.agents.metering_caption: What each agent did and spent in the last 30 days
app.agents.metering_empty: No agent has acted in the last 30 days.
app.provenance.field.title: Title
app.ai.title: AI
app.ai.intro: Which provider this workspace asks, under which models, and whether its content may be sent there at all. Choosing a provider and consenting to use it are two decisions, and both are made here.
app.ai.none: This workspace has no AI provider. Nothing here proposes anything until one is configured and consented to.
app.ai.kind_hint: OpenAI-compatible covers OpenAI, Azure, Mistral, vLLM and LiteLLM. Ollama is a model running where you run it. None calls nothing.
app.ai.base_url_hint: Where the provider is reached. Leave it empty for the provider’s own default.
app.ai.base_url_hint_required: Where the provider is reached. An offered model needs one: every workspace that chooses it is sent there.
app.ai.completion_model_hint: The model that writes titles, notes, breakdowns and summaries, named as the provider names it.
app.ai.embedding_model_hint: The model that turns entries into vectors for search by meaning and for finding look-alikes. Leave it empty to search by words only.
app.ai.api_key_hint: Sealed as soon as it is saved. Nothing shows it again.
app.ai.api_key_kept: A key is stored. Leave this empty to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
app.ai.jurisdiction_label: Where the provider processes what it is sent
app.ai.jurisdiction_hint: Declared by you, recorded with the configuration, and shown to the people whose content goes there.
app.ai.jurisdiction_needed: Choose where it processes content first.
app.ai.jurisdiction_adequacy: In a country with an adequacy decision
app.ai.consent_label: Send this workspace’s content to the provider
app.ai.consent_label_named: Send this workspace’s content to {host}, {where, select, SELF_HOSTED {on this installation’s own infrastructure} EEA {in the EEA} ADEQUACY {in a country with an adequacy decision} other {in a third country}}
app.ai.consent_hint: With this on, an entry’s title and notes, the comments on it, an arrival’s subject and body, and the names of a collection’s labels and columns are sent to the provider named above whenever somebody asks for a proposal, a summary or a search by meaning. Nothing is sent while it is off, and nothing is ever sent without somebody asking.
app.ai.rebuilding: Search by meaning is being rebuilt for the model now in use. Search by words works meanwhile.
app.ai.none_allowed: This workspace uses no AI: {by}. Everything else works as before.
app.ai.offered_sent_to: Your content is sent to {processor} {where, select, SELF_HOSTED {on this installation’s own infrastructure} EEA {in the EEA} ADEQUACY {in a country with an adequacy decision} other {in a third country}} when somebody asks for a suggestion, a summary or a search by meaning - and only then.
app.ai.use_own_hint: The model configured below answers instead, under its own consent.
app.ai.own_not_allowed: Only the model your provider offers may be used here: {by}. A model of your own is not offered.
app.ai.minimum: Your own model must process content {minimum, select, ADEQUACY {in the EEA or a country with an adequacy decision} EEA {in the EEA} SELF_HOSTED {on this installation’s own infrastructure} other {where this installation allows}}: {by}.
app.ai.narrow_hint: Narrow what this workspace allows itself. No AI is always possible.
app.ai.narrow_either: The offered model or our own
app.ai.sources_locked: Which AI this workspace may use is {by}.
app.ai.set_by_installation: set for every workspace on this installation
app.ai.arrival_label: Prepare proposals for new jumble entries
app.ai.arrival_hint: AI reads each new entry when it arrives and leaves a proposal on its card. This uses the workspace's AI budget, up to a daily number of entries.
app.ai.arrival_on_announced: New jumble entries get a proposal.
app.ai.arrival_off_announced: New jumble entries wait for somebody to ask.
app.ai.opt_out_intro: Whether each person here may keep what they wrote out of AI. AI stays this workspace's decision; a person can only keep their own content out.
app.ai.opt_out_offered: Each person may keep their own content out of AI
app.ai.opt_out_not_offered: AI is part of everybody's work
app.ai.opt_out_basis_hint: Everybody here sees it instead of the switch. Hubtask records the basis and shows it; whether it holds is yours to judge.

app.import.kind_CSV_hint: A header row and one entry per line, saved as CSV from any spreadsheet. Columns named title, notes, due, completed, labels, bucket or parent are taken as such; the next step lets you name the others.

app.import.mapping_hint: The file's columns, one per field. Where a header already names a field it is filled in; leave a field empty to ignore it.
app.import.no_header: No header row could be read from the file. The import will still try, and refuses the file if it cannot read one either.
