app.backup.title: Backup
app.backup.intro: Where this workspace's archives are written, what runs on its own, and which of them has been opened since it was made.
app.backup.reading_archives: Reading what is at the target
app.backup.no_targets: No target is configured, so nothing is being backed up.
app.backup.target_path_hint: Relative to the volume this installation writes backups inside.
app.backup.target_host_key_hint: The server's public key as ssh-keyscan prints it, or its SHA256 fingerprint. Required: a server nobody named is never trusted.
app.backup.target_private_key_hint: The key the server knows this installation by, as OpenSSH or PEM prints it - instead of the password or beside it.
app.backup.target_url_hint: The WebDAV folder's full address, beginning with https://. User and password go in their own fields.
app.backup.target_region_hint: Where the bucket is, such as eu-central-1. Empty means us-east-1.
app.backup.encryption_hint: Encrypted, an archive is unreadable to whoever runs the target. Not encrypted, anybody who can read the target can read the workspace.
app.backup.insecure_title: This target leaves the workspace unprotected
app.backup.insecure_accept: I accept this and want the target anyway.
app.backup.insecure_first: Accept the risk above first, or change the target.
app.backup.target_needed: Choose the target the schedule writes to.
app.backup.credentials_write_only: Credentials are stored sealed and are never answered back. To change one, type it again.
app.backup.never_tested: This target has never been tested.
app.backup.tested_failed: Last tested {at}, and it did not answer.
app.backup.probe_ok: Wrote, read and deleted a file in {ms} ms.
app.backup.probe_failed: The target could not be reached.
app.backup.probe_not_writable: It can be read and not written, which is a permission at the target rather than here.
app.backup.progress_unknown: How far along is not knowable yet
app.backup.cancel_note: Stopping is a request rather than a kill: the run stops at its next write, and bytes already at the target stay there.
app.backup.verify_done: The archive's checksums matched and it opens.
app.backup.hide_archives: Hide what is at this target
app.backup.no_archives: Nothing has been written here yet.
app.backup.last_verified: An archive here was last checked {at}.
app.backup.never_verified: No archive here has ever been checked. “We have backups” and “we have backups that open” are different claims.
app.backup.remove_note: The archives already written stay where they are; only this workspace's way of reaching them goes. A target a schedule still names is refused.
app.backup.schedules_intro: What runs without anybody asking, and when it next will.
app.backup.no_schedules: Nothing runs on its own. Every archive here was asked for by hand.
app.backup.schedule_rule_hint: RFC 5545, without the RRULE: prefix — FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=3;BYMINUTE=0
app.backup.schedule_min_keep_hint: The floor under every generation. A retention rule may never leave no backup at all.
app.backup.rule_is_the_servers: When the rule next falls is worked out on the server. This screen reads the rule and expands nothing.
app.backup.no_next_run_off: Switched off, so nothing is owed.
app.backup.no_next_run_spent: The rule has no occurrence left. It is spent rather than broken.
app.backup.remove_schedule_note: No backup is taken on it from tonight on, and its rule, zone and generations go with it. The archives it wrote stay where they are. Switching it off instead keeps all of it.
app.backup.switch_off_rather_than_delete: Switching it off keeps the rule, the zone and the generations for the night somebody wants them back.
app.backup.min_keep: Never fewer than {count} archives, whatever the generations say.
app.backup.tested_announced: Target tested; the outcome is beside it.
app.restore.title: Restore
app.restore.intro: Putting an archive back. Every restore is rehearsed first: you see what it would do before anything happens.
app.restore.operators_title: Two ways in are the operator's
app.restore.operators_note: Restoring into a new workspace, or restoring the whole installation, crosses or creates a workspace and is not something one workspace can do. Ask whoever runs this installation.
app.restore.reading_archives: Reading what is at the target
app.restore.archive_incomplete: That archive is unfinished — the run that wrote it did not get to the end. Restoring from it is possible and what comes back is partial.
app.restore.mode_inspect_note: Reads the archive and reports what is in it. Nothing here changes, ever.
app.restore.mode_selective_note: Only the collections and entries you name come back. Everything else is left as it is.
app.restore.mode_merge_note: Everything in the archive is brought back beside what is here. What happens to a collision is the rule below.
app.restore.mode_replace_tenant_note: Everything here is replaced by what is in the archive. This is the only way in that removes things.
app.restore.selection_note: Named from what this workspace has now. Only what you tick comes back from the archive; everything else is left alone.
app.restore.conflict_rule_hint: What to do about an entry the archive holds and this workspace already has.
app.restore.conflict_overwrite: Replace it with the archive's version
app.restore.conflict_duplicate: Bring the archive's version back beside it
app.restore.replace_title: This replaces everything in this workspace
app.restore.replace_note: Every entry, collection, comment and attachment here is replaced by what the archive holds. Anything created since the archive was written is gone.
app.restore.credentials_note: Sign-in credentials do not survive this. The accounts, sessions and access tokens that can reach this workspace are among the rows being replaced, so you may not be able to sign back in afterwards — including with the account you are using now.
app.restore.acknowledge_cost: I have read what this replaces, and that sign-in credentials do not survive it
app.restore.type_name: Type the workspace's name — {name} — to confirm
app.restore.type_name_hint: Exactly as it is written. This is the confirmation the server asks for.
app.restore.safety_backup: Take a copy of this workspace first
app.restore.safety_backup_hint: On by default, and this is the way back. The copy is written to the same target before anything is replaced.
app.restore.no_safety_note: Without it there is no way back: what is here now is gone the moment the restore runs, and nothing will hold it.
app.restore.acknowledge_no_safety: I understand there will be no way back
app.restore.target_needed: Choose the target the archive is on.
app.restore.archive_needed: Choose the archive to bring back.
app.restore.selection_needed: Tick at least one hub to bring back.
app.restore.name_needed: Type the workspace's name exactly as it is written.
app.restore.safety_needed: Keep the safety copy, or confirm that you give it up.
app.restore.rehearse_note: This is a rehearsal. It reads the archive, works out what would happen, and writes nothing.
app.restore.rehearsing_title: Working out what it would do
app.restore.progress_unknown: How far along is not knowable yet
app.restore.report_new: Brought back and not here now: {count}.
app.restore.report_duplicated: Brought back beside what is here: {count}.
app.restore.report_deleted: Kept out because they were deleted since: {count}.
app.restore.withheld_deletion_journal: Deliberately not brought back, because they were deleted after the archive was written: {count}.
app.restore.withheld_excluded_entity: Deliberately not brought back, because a restore never brings them: {count}.
app.restore.replace_held_title: A legal hold is in force
app.restore.replace_held: While a legal hold is in force in this workspace, it cannot be reset to a backup. You can still rehearse the replace to see what it would do; it runs once every hold is released.
app.restore.withheld_legal_hold_kept: {count, plural, one {# legal hold of the archive was} other {# legal holds of the archive were}} not taken over: the workspace keeps its own holds as they are.
app.restore.rehearsal_failed: The rehearsal did not finish, so there is nothing to read
app.restore.rehearsal_wrote_nothing: Nothing has happened yet. This is what would happen.
app.restore.run_for_real_note: This runs exactly what you just read — the same archive, the same way in, the same choices.
app.restore.safety_taken: A copy of this workspace was taken first. Its run identifier is {id}.
app.identity_provider.title: Sign-in providers
app.identity_provider.intro: Your organisation's own providers can sign people in here. Password sign-in keeps working alongside them, which is what keeps this workspace reachable when a provider is not.
app.identity_provider.not_served: This installation does not offer provider sign-in.
app.identity_provider.none: No provider is configured. Add one and people can sign in through it.
app.identity_provider.inherited_intro: Everybody on this installation can sign in through these. Only its operator can change them.
app.identity_provider.switched_in_sign_i: A provider is switched on or off for this workspace under Sign-in, in the list of ways to sign in. A new one is saved off.
app.identity_provider.registration: What to do at the provider
app.identity_provider.kind_hint: This decides the mark on the sign-in button and what the provider is allowed to do here. Hubtask checks it against the issuer you give, so a mark cannot end up over somebody else's provider.
app.identity_provider.name_hint: What people read on the sign-in card. Left empty it is the issuer's host, which is where the button sends them anyway.
app.identity_provider.provisioning_label: Who may sign in through it?
app.identity_provider.provisioning_hint: Only what this provider may do is offered. Only people invited here gives nobody a new account; the other two give one to whoever they let in.
app.identity_provider.newcomers_hint: Given with the account, the first time somebody arrives through this provider. People who already have an account here keep what they have.
app.identity_provider.newcomers_nothing: No access until an administrator gives it
app.identity_provider.newcomers_role: The role {role} on the whole workspace
app.identity_provider.directories_shared: Required: this address stands for every organisation at the provider, so only people from the directories named here may sign in through it.
app.identity_provider.directories_narrow: Optional. One per line: only invited people from these may sign in through this provider. Left empty, every invited person may.
app.identity_provider.redirect_hint: Enter it at the provider exactly as shown.
app.identity_provider.issuer_hint: The https address the provider identifies itself by. Hubtask fetches its metadata before saving, so an address it cannot reach is refused here rather than by the first person who tries to sign in.
app.identity_provider.client_id_hint: What this Hubtask is registered as at the provider.
app.identity_provider.client_secret_hint: Sealed when it is saved. There is no way to read it back afterwards, by design.
app.identity_provider.client_secret_kept: A secret is already sealed for this provider. Leave this empty to keep it, or type a new one to replace it. It is never shown again either way.
app.identity_provider.domains_hint: One per line. Nobody outside them gets in through this provider, and somebody inside them who has no account here yet is given one. An empty list admits nobody, because the list is the setting.
app.identity_provider.directories_label_: Microsoft directories that may sign in
app.identity_provider.directories_hint_t: One directory id per line. This is the value Microsoft calls the tenant id, and it is what decides who gets in - the email address is not, because Microsoft says its own email claim must never be used for that. Personal Microsoft accounts belong to no organisation here: they come in only by invitation. An empty list lets nobody in.
app.identity_provider.directories_label_: Google Workspace domains that may sign in
app.identity_provider.directories_hint_h: One domain per line, as Google reports it. Google is explicit that the email address's domain is not enough to tell whether an organisation runs that account - this is the value that is, and it is what decides who gets in. An empty list lets nobody in, and a personal Google account belongs to no domain at all.
app.identity_provider.shared_endpoint: This provider also has shared addresses - common for every directory and every personal account, organizations for work accounts, consumers for personal ones. Use one and a single registration serves everybody you name below; use one directory's own address and it serves that one. A personal account comes in only by invitation, whichever address you use.
app.identity_provider.saved: Saved. The provider answered its metadata.
app.identity_provider.remove_cost: Everybody the provider signed in keeps their account, their work and the session they are in right now. What they lose is the way back in: somebody who has only ever signed in through the provider has no password to fall back on, and will need an invitation to set one.
app.identity_provider.remove_confirm: This removes the configuration and its sealed secret. Setting it up again means typing the secret again.
app.step_up.title: Prove it is you
app.step_up.why: Hubtask asks again before a step like this one. Nothing is changed until you answer.
app.step_up.code_hint: Six digits, the one showing now.
app.step_up.recovery_hint: One of the ten you stored. Using it here uses it up.
app.step_up.with_code: Use the code from your authenticator
app.step_up.provider_leaving: You sign in at {provider} once more, and come back here.
app.step_up.confirmed: Confirmed with {provider}. Do what you were about to do again - it goes through now.
app.step_up.no_method: This account holds no way to confirm this here: no password, no second factor and no provider switched on in this workspace. An administrator of this workspace can help.
app.step_up.provider_in_browser: This account confirms with a fresh sign-in at its provider, which takes a browser - a terminal cannot do it. Do this in the web app instead.
app.sign_out.everywhere_else_note: This ends every other session of your account, on every other device and browser. You stay signed in here.
app.redeem.title: Set your password
app.redeem.intro: You were invited to this workspace. Choose a password and you are in.
app.redeem.invited_intro: You were invited. Choose a password and you are in.
app.redeem.provider_intro: This workspace signs in through its provider, not with a password. Sign in there with the address the invitation went to, and you are in.
app.redeem.or_provider: Or accept it by signing in through the workspace's provider, with the address the invitation went to.
app.redeem.submit: Set the password and sign in
app.redeem.password_short: A password is at least twelve characters.
app.redeem.no_token: This link carries no invitation. Open the invitation link you were sent again; it works once.
app.sessions.title: Where you are signed in
app.sessions.intro: Every session your account holds. Ending one takes effect on its next request.
app.sessions.none: There is nothing to show, which should not happen while you are signed in.
app.devices.title: Devices that synchronise
app.devices.intro: Every device that holds a copy of this workspace for your account. Forgetting one refuses its next synchronisation; the device then starts over with a fresh copy.
app.devices.confirm_body: Its next synchronisation is refused and it starts over with a fresh copy of the workspace. What it has not sent yet, it keeps for you to look at there.
app.sessions.end_confirm_body: Whoever is signed in on {client} is signed out at once. An ended session cannot be resumed; signing in again opens a new one.
app.sessions.this_confirm_title: End the session on this device?
app.sessions.this_confirm_body: You are signed out here at once. Signing in again opens a new session.
app.sessions.others_confirm_body: Every other session ends at once and cannot be resumed. You stay signed in here.
app.grants.withdraw_confirm_body: {app} can no longer act for you, from now on. To use it again, you allow it again when it asks.
app.tokens.revoke_confirm_body: Whatever uses {name} stops working at once. A withdrawn token cannot be restored; you can make a new one.
app.maturity.experimental.title: Hubtask is experimental
app.maturity.experimental.body: Screens appear, move and disappear without notice, and nothing here is a commitment yet.
app.maturity.preview.title: Hubtask is a preview
app.maturity.preview.body: What you see is meant to stay. What is still missing is listed in the release notes.
app.installation.title: This installation
app.installation.unread: This installation could not be read, so this client does not know what it permits.
app.health.title: This installation is not working fully
app.offline: Hubtask cannot reach the server. Check the connection and try again.
app.offline.as_of: Shown from this device's copy, as of {moment}. It refreshes when the server can be reached again.
app.request_timed_out: The server took too long to answer. Try again.
app.answer_unreadable: The server sent an answer this version of Hubtask cannot read.
app.something_went_wrong: Something went wrong. Try again in a moment.
app.shell.nothing_to_do: There is nothing to do here yet.
app.undo.label_deleted: {name} is deleted. The entries that carried it carry it again if you undo.
app.undo.bulk_trashed: {count, plural, one {# entry is} other {# entries are}} in the trash.
app.undo.bulk_label_removed: The label is off {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
app.entry_menu.label: Actions for {title}
app.rank.already_first: This is already first in its list.
app.rank.already_last: This is already last in its list.
app.move.nothing_above: There is nothing above this one to move it inside.
app.move.already_top: This is already at the top level of its collection.
app.move.choose_first: Choose a collection to move it to first.
app.move.no_destination: There is no other collection in this workspace to move it to.
app.move.leaves_behind: Labels and the board column belong to the collection an entry is in, so they stay behind. You will be told exactly what did.
app.move.dropped_kind.LABEL: Label
app.board.moved_over_limit: {title} moved to {name}, which now holds more than its limit of {limit}.
app.move.choose_hub_first: Choose a hub to move it to first.
app.move.no_hub: There is no other hub in this workspace to move it to.
app.view.label: How these entries are shown
app.view.not_built: This installation offers {layout}, and this version of the client cannot draw it yet.
app.query.title: Which entries to show
app.query.none_filterable: This installation reports no field that can be filtered on.
app.search.title: Search
app.search.narrowed_none: Nothing here matches what you narrowed it to.
app.search.label: Search the entries you can see
app.search.hint: Quoted phrases, or between words and a leading minus all work.
app.search.copy_link: Copy a link to this search
app.search.link_carries: A link carries what you narrowed the search to. The words you typed stay on this device.
app.search.start: Type to search the entries you can see.
app.search.partial: These are the first results. Narrow the words to see the rest.
app.entries.archived: This entry is archived, so nothing on it can be changed. Unarchive it to work on it again.
app.entries.archived_ask: This entry is archived, so nothing on it can be changed. Ask whoever may change it to unarchive it.
app.celebration.parent: {title} is done, and with it everything under its parent.
app.celebration.collection: {title} is done. Nothing is left open in this collection.
app.celebration.hub: {title} is done. Nothing is left open in this hub.
app.celebration.day: {title} is done, and that was the last thing due today.
app.celebration.first: {title} is done. That was your first.
app.help.label: Help and shortcuts
app.shortcuts.group.palette: In the search and command list
app.shortcuts.group.list: On a list or a board
app.shortcuts.palette_move: Move to the next or the previous row
app.shortcuts.palette_enter: Open the chosen row, or all results
app.shortcuts.palette_escape: Close the list and go back where you were
app.shortcuts.rank_step: Move the entry one place up or down
app.shortcuts.rank_end: Move the entry to the top or the bottom
app.shortcuts.select_one: Select an entry, or take it out of the selection
app.shortcuts.select_range: Select every entry up to this one
app.tour.hubs.caption: Where work lives
app.tour.hubs.body: A hub holds collections, and a collection holds the entries. Everything you make sits somewhere in this tree, and the tree is the same on every screen.
app.tour.capture.caption: Catch it before it slips
app.tour.capture.body: Capture takes a line from any page, or press Q. Say where it goes, or leave it in the jumble and decide later.
app.tour.palette.caption: Find anything, do anything
app.tour.palette.body: Type to find an entry, a hub or a command. Ctrl+K or ⌘K opens this from anywhere, and ? lists every shortcut.
app.tour.levels.caption: Smaller steps under it
app.tour.levels.body: An entry can hold the work under it, one level at a time. How many levels there are is up to the collection's structure.
app.tour.layouts.caption: The same entries, more than one way
app.tour.layouts.body: A collection draws its entries as a list, a board or a timeline, as far as its structure offers them — the same entries each time. Switch here; nothing moves but your view.
app.tour.entry.caption: What an entry carries
app.tour.entry.body: A title, notes, a due date, labels, the people on it, and the work under it. Everything about one thing, on one screen.
app.tour.jumble.caption: Where things arrive before they are work
app.tour.jumble.body: What you capture without a collection, forward or dictate lands here first. Nothing in the jumble is a task yet; you decide what becomes one.
app.tour.search.caption: Ask for entries in one line
app.tour.search.body: Words find titles and notes. Add is:open, due:today or label:name to narrow it — the whole query language fits in this field.
app.tour.profile.caption: Yours to set
app.tour.profile.body: Language, time zone and the first day of the week follow you, wherever you sign in. The theme, the motion and the moments are on the next row of this column, because they belong to the device in front of you.
app.tour.make.caption: Now make one
app.tour.make.body: Add an entry and tick it off. That first completion is the moment this tour has been leading to.
app.entries.created_lines_announced: {count, plural, one {# entry was added} other {# entries were added}}.
app.archive.title: Archive
app.archive.intro: What has been put aside here. An archived hub or collection is read-only and out of the navigation; it keeps everything in it and comes back the way it went.
app.archive.none_body: Archiving a hub or a collection takes it out of the navigation and leaves everything in it where it is. What is archived appears here.
app.archive.entries: Archived entries stay in the list they belong to and say so there. The search lists all of them at once.
app.trash.title: Trash
app.trash.empty_body: This cannot be undone. Deletions listed here: {count}. Each takes everything that went in with it. Nothing under a legal hold is removed.
app.trash.window: Days left before it goes for good: {days}.
app.trash.window_unknown: Your workspace decides how long this is kept.
app.trash.window_restricted: Kept because the person's data is restricted.
app.trash.batch: Everything deleted with it comes back too.
app.trash.partial: These are the first of what is in the trash.
app.trash.empty_title: Delete everything in the trash for good?
app.trash.purge_body: This cannot be undone. Everything that was deleted with it goes too, and no backup brings it back.
app.trash.again: A large trash takes more than one pass. Empty it again to continue.
app.trash.blocked.legal_hold: a legal hold is in force on them
app.trash.blocked.tombstone_window: they were deleted too recently for the deletion journal
app.trash.purge_container: A hub or a collection goes for good when the trash is emptied, or when the retention period runs out.
app.retention.title: Retention and holds
app.retention.intro: What this workspace removes on its own once something is old enough — and the instructions that stop it.
app.retention.no_rules: Nothing is removed on a schedule. Everything here stays until somebody deletes it.
app.retention.failing: Since {at} its condition could not be evaluated on an entry, so this rule announces and removes nothing until a pass evaluates it again. The workspace's other rules go on.
app.retention.justified: Kept longer than the ceiling because: {reason}
app.retention.action_notify_only: Only report what it would remove
app.retention.preview_first: Look at what it would do first.
app.retention.preview_share: share of what is here: {percent} per cent
app.retention.preview_broad: That is more than a twentieth of this workspace. A new rule this wide is stored as an announcement rather than switched on, whatever it says.
app.retention.preview_wrote_nothing: Looking changes nothing. Nothing has been removed.
app.retention.blocked_legal_hold: Held back by a legal hold, and not touched: {count}.
app.retention.blocked_restriction: Held back because the person's data is restricted: {count}.
app.retention.blocked_tombstone_window: Held back inside the window that keeps a deletion visible to other devices: {count}.
app.retention.withdraw_note: Withdrawing stops the rule. What it already removed stays removed — a deletion is not undone by withdrawing the instruction behind it.
app.retention.landed_title: This rule was stored as an announcement
app.retention.landed_note: You asked for “{asked}”. Its first run would affect more than a twentieth of this workspace, so it was stored reporting rather than removing. Look at what it would do, then change it if that is what you meant.
app.retention.write_note: A new rule is written switched off and shown to you first. Nothing is removed until you switch it on.
app.retention.kind_not_swept: This installation names that class of data but removes nothing of it, so a rule for it would be refused.
app.retention.kind.COMPLETED_ITEM: Completed tasks, work packages and activities
app.retention.kind.OPEN_ITEM_STALE: Open work nobody has changed for a long time
app.retention.kind.JUMBLE_ENTRY: Jumble entries that never became work
app.retention.kind.RULE_RUN: The record of what rules did
app.retention.kind.MEDIA_ORPHAN: Files nothing refers to any more
app.retention.days_hint: Days from the moment the clock starts for this class of data.
app.retention.days_hint_ceiling: Days. Beyond {days} this installation asks for a reason, and keeps it.
app.retention.justification_hint: A sentence somebody will read in an audit. Only needed when the period exceeds this installation's ceiling.
app.retention.effective_intro: The rules that would actually act on what is inside one place, inheritance included. It is rarely the rule written at that level.
app.retention.holds_intro: A hold is the first thing every deletion checks, and it outranks every rule above. It is here rather than on a page of its own because this is where somebody reads what would otherwise happen.
app.retention.show_released: Show the ones that were lifted
app.retention.hide_released: Hide the ones that were lifted
app.retention.hold_scope_container: One hub or collection, and everything in it
app.retention.hold_scope_item: One entry, and everything under it
app.retention.hold_person_note: Their account and the entries, comments and files they contributed are kept from deletion - an erasure of them included. They can still sign in.
app.retention.hold_covers_entry: The entry “{title}”, and everything under it
app.retention.hold_covers_entry_unnamed: One entry, and everything under it
app.retention.hold_reason_hint: Required, and kept. This is what an auditor reads when they ask why something was not deleted.
app.retention.hold_not_retain: A hold is not the same as keeping one entry: keeping takes a single entry out of a running period, a hold overrides every rule and reaches everything below it.
app.activity.title: History
app.people.title: People
app.comments.title: Comments
app.comments.none: Nothing has been said about this entry yet. Start the conversation.
app.comments.none_closed: Nothing has been said about this entry.
app.comments.reply_to_removed: That comment was removed, so it cannot be replied to.
app.comments.too_long: A comment holds at most {limit} characters; this one has {length}.
app.people.intro: Who holds a role at this workspace itself. A role granted here reaches everything in it; roles granted on a hub or a collection are managed where they were granted.
app.people.grant_hint: A role at the workspace applies to everything in it. Granting or revoking Owner asks you to prove it is you first.
app.people.invite_hint: They get an email with a link, choose a password, and are in. The role you pick applies to the whole workspace and can be changed afterwards.
app.people.invite_hint_link: No mail goes out from here. You get a link to hand over yourself, by any messenger; it works once, for fourteen days. They open it, choose a password, and are in. The role you pick applies to the whole workspace and can be changed afterwards.
app.people.invite_hint_neutral: They get a link, choose a password, and are in. The role you pick applies to the whole workspace and can be changed afterwards.
app.people.invite_link_hint: Shown only now. Hand it over by any messenger; it works once, for fourteen days, and any earlier link for this person no longer works. Lost it? Renew the invitation from the list.
app.people.invite_link_keep_first: Copy the link first: it cannot be shown again.
app.people.invite_name_hint: Optional. Without one they are shown by their address until they set a name.
app.people.invite_role_hint: Required here: an invitation on its own gives somebody access to nothing, and nobody would see them.
app.people.invited_here: Invitation sent to {email}, with the role here and nowhere else.
app.people.renewed_here: The invitation to {name} went out again; the earlier link no longer works.
app.people.invite_where_hint: The whole workspace, or one hub: somebody invited to a hub sees that hub and nothing else of the workspace.
app.people.invited_sent: Invitation sent to {email}. They appear below as invited until they arrive.
app.groups.title: Groups
app.groups.intro: A group is a way to give several people the same role at once. Grant a role to the group, and everybody in it holds it.
app.groups.name: Name
app.groups.name_hint: What this group is called, wherever it is named.
app.groups.above_own: This group gives a role you do not hold yourself, so only someone who holds it may change who is in the group or delete it.
app.groups.delete_cost: Deleting the group takes its roles with it: whatever it granted, nobody holds afterwards. The people stay; what they could do through this group stops.
app.permissions.title: What each role means
app.permissions.intro: As this installation enforces it. Nothing here is set by hand — a role is granted, and this says what the grant means.
app.permissions.unknown: This installation has not said what its roles carry yet.
app.permissions.assigned_note: “Assigned only” means an entry the person is the assignee of. A contributor may create anything and change what is theirs — a created entry is assigned to whoever created it, so the two do not contradict each other.
app.service_accounts.title: Service accounts
app.service_accounts.intro: An account that is nobody: no address, no sign-in, tokens as its only credential. It is what an integration or an automation rule should run as, so that neither stops working when the person who set it up leaves.
app.service_accounts.name: Name
app.service_accounts.name_hint: Name it after what it does — “the nightly export”, not “svc1”. It is what a reader of the audit trail sees.
app.service_accounts.then_grant: A new service account holds nothing. Give it a role under People, then mint it a token here.
app.service_accounts.no_roles: This account holds no role, so its tokens will be accepted and then refused by everything. Give it a role under People.
app.service_accounts.created_announced: Service account created; its secret is shown once.
app.grants.title: Apps you have allowed
app.grants.intro: Third-party apps that can act in this workspace as you, bounded by what you gave them and by what you can do yourself.
app.grants.next_request: Withdrawing takes effect on the app's next request. Anything it is doing at that moment finishes.
app.apps.title: Third-party apps
app.apps.intro: Apps registered here can ask people in this workspace to let them act as them. Each person decides for themselves and can withdraw it afterwards.
app.apps.name: Name
app.apps.name_hint: What people read when they decide whether to allow it. Name it after what it is, not after the company.
app.apps.uris_hint: One per line, matched exactly — character for character, including the trailing slash or the lack of one. An address that differs by one character is refused.
app.apps.is_confidential: This app can keep a secret
app.apps.is_confidential_hint: True for an app that runs on a server it controls: it gets a secret, shown once. False for a native or single-page app, which cannot keep one — it proves itself with PKCE instead. Choosing wrong is how a secret ends up in a bundle anybody can read.
app.apps.remove_cost: Removing the app withdraws everything people allowed it. Whatever it is running stops on its next request, and everybody who allowed it would have to allow it again.
app.apps.secret_hint: Shown once. Nothing can show it again — give it to whoever runs the app and store it where they keep their other secrets.
app.apps.no_secret: Registered. This app gets no secret: it proves itself with PKCE, which is what a native or single-page app can actually keep.
app.apps.keep_first: Save the secret first. It cannot be shown again.
app.apps.registered_announced: App registered; its secret is shown once.
app.machines.title: Machines and apps
app.jumble.title: Jumble
app.jumble.intro: Things that arrived by mail, by webhook, or that you captured without a collection. Each one becomes an entry or is dismissed — and a dismissal keeps it readable rather than deleting it.
app.jumble.arrived: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing more arrived.} one {# more arrival is listed.} other {# more arrivals are listed.}}
app.jumble.dismissed_note: Dismissed, not deleted. It stays readable here until the retention rule removes it.
app.jumble.ask: Ask AI what this should become
app.jumble.select_first: Select the entries to ask about first.
app.jumble.selection_asked: AI is asked about the selected entries.
app.jumble.selection_some_failed: {count, plural, one {# entry could not be asked about.} other {# entries could not be asked about.}}
app.jumble.destination_hint: A collection you can write in. The entry is created there, and this arrival then points at it.
app.jumble.entry_title_hint: The subject, unless you want something else.
app.jumble.intake_hint: Mail and webhooks reach this workspace through an address that carries a secret. It is shown when it is made and never again, so making a new one is the only way to see one.
app.jumble.intake_minted_hint: Shown once. Put it into whatever posts here, and treat it like a password — anybody who has it can put things in this jumble.
app.jumble.rotate_cost: The address in use now stops working the moment you do this. Anything that posts to it — a mail rule, a webhook, a script — has to be given the new one.
app.jumble.keep_first: Save the address first. It cannot be shown again.
app.jumble.rotated_announced: A new address was made; the old one stops working.
app.runs.title: What the rules did
app.runs.intro: Every run and why it ended the way it did. A rule is tried and started in its editor.
app.runs.arrived: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing more arrived.} one {# more run arrived.} other {# more runs arrived.}}
app.runs.skipped_by: Condition {index} did not hold, so the rule did nothing. That is not a failure.
app.runs.throttled_note: The rule had already run as often as it is allowed to this hour. It protected the workspace from itself.
app.runs.aborted_note: A rule set off another, {depth} deep, and the engine stopped the chain before it became a loop.
app.runs.crashed_note: This run says it is still going and started a long time ago, which means the process handling it stopped. It is not progressing.
app.runs.replay_note: This finishes the run that failed rather than starting a new one. {count} actions already succeeded and will not be done again — nothing gets sent twice.
app.webhooks.title: Webhooks
app.webhooks.intro: An external system's standing request to be told what happens here — and the log of every attempt to tell it.
app.webhooks.none: Nothing subscribes to this workspace's events.
app.webhooks.failing_note: Deliveries that failed in a row, most recently: {count}. A run of them switches the subscription off.
app.webhooks.disabled_note: This was switched off after a run of failed deliveries, of which there were {count}. Nothing has been delivered since; switching it back on resumes from the next event, not from what was missed.
app.webhooks.target_url_hint: The address the event is posted to. It must be reachable from this installation.
app.webhooks.format_hint: The signed event for a server you run, or a sentence for a team's chat room.
app.webhooks.target_url_hint_matrix: The homeserver's address, such as https://matrix.example.org.
app.webhooks.target_url_hint_room: The room's incoming webhook address. It is kept sealed, and only its server is shown afterwards.
app.webhooks.room_hint: The room identifier from the room's settings, starting with “!”.
app.webhooks.credential_hint: The token of the account that posts the notices. It is kept sealed and never shown again.
app.webhooks.locale_hint: The language the room is told in, such as de. Empty is the installation's language.
app.webhooks.types_unknown: This installation has not said yet which events it emits.
app.webhooks.types_note: These are the events this installation emits. A type it does not emit is refused rather than stored, so a subscription cannot wait for something that will never arrive.
app.webhooks.egress_note: Whether an address can be reached is this installation's decision, not this screen's: a private address is refused unless the installation deliberately allows them, and the refusal appears here.
app.webhooks.secret_hint: Shown once. Every delivery is signed with it, and the subscriber checks the signature — there is no read that answers it again. Store it before you close this.
app.webhooks.kept: I have stored it somewhere safe
app.webhooks.keep_first: Store it first — this is the only time it exists outside the server.
app.webhooks.rotate_note: Deliveries are signed with the new secret from the moment you press this. The old one keeps verifying at the subscriber for as long as you choose below, which is the time they have to deploy it.
app.webhooks.grace: How long the old secret keeps verifying
app.webhooks.grace_hint: A subscriber cannot deploy at the same instant you press the button. This is the window that covers the gap.
app.webhooks.grace_604800: Seven days — the longest this contract allows
app.webhooks.grace_0: At once — what a leaked secret calls for, and what drops anything signed before the subscriber has the new one
app.webhooks.unsubscribe_note: The delivery log goes with it: a record of attempts against an address this workspace no longer knows is a record of nothing.
app.webhooks.no_deliveries: Nothing has been delivered to this subscription.
app.webhooks.scope_hint: A hub includes its collections. An event about no hub or collection, such as a rule run, reaches only a subscription of the whole workspace.
app.webhooks.scope_unseen: A hub or collection you do not see
app.webhooks.condition_hint: A condition every event must meet to be sent, written as in a rule. It may name event, data (what the receiver gets), actor and now, for example data.title.startsWith("Ship"). Leave it empty to send every event.
app.webhooks.outcome_filter_failed: Held back: the condition could not be judged
app.webhooks.replay_note: Sending it again carries the same event identifier, so a subscriber that recognises repeats sees this for what it is. The attempt count carries on rather than starting over.
app.webhooks.arrived: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing more arrived.} one {# more delivery is listed.} other {# more deliveries are listed.}}
app.webhooks.subscribed_announced: Subscribed; the secret is shown once.
app.webhooks.rotated_announced: Secret rotated; the new one is shown once.
app.rules.title: Automation
app.rules.intro: Rules that do something when something happens. Each runs as an account and can never do more than that account may.
app.rules.created_off: A rule is created switched off. You will be able to read it back before letting it loose.
app.rules.name: Name
app.rules.scope_hint: A rule on a hub sees what happens in its collections too — the same way a role granted on a hub applies downwards.
app.rules.scope_hub: The hub {name}, and everything in it
app.rules.runs_as_hint: The rule acts with this account's rights and can never exceed them. A service account is what this usually should be: it does not leave when a person does.
app.rules.trigger_step_taken: A step of a workflow is taken
app.rules.event_type_hint: What this installation publishes. One it does not publish is refused by name.
app.rules.rrule_hint: An RFC 5545 rule, such as FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO.
app.rules.timezone_hint: Required for a schedule: without one, “every Monday at seven” means something different in summer.
app.rules.conditions_hint: Expressions that all have to hold. None means the rule runs on every match. They are compiled when you save, so a mistake is caught here rather than at three in the morning.
app.rules.actions_hint: At least one. They run in order, and a branch's two arms are checked exactly as this list is.
app.rules.action_params_hint: As JSON. A key the action does not take is refused by name when you save.
app.rules.wait_duration_hint: An ISO 8601 duration of at most a year, such as PT1H or P1D. Nothing is held open while it waits.
app.rules.branch_condition_hint: An expression. When it holds, the first list runs; otherwise the second.
app.rules.stop_hint: Ends the run here. Everything after it is marked skipped, and the run counts as succeeded — stopping early is what the rule said to do.
app.rules.max_runs: At most this many runs an hour
app.rules.max_runs_hint: Optional. What stops a rule from turning one busy afternoon into a thousand runs.
app.rules.dedupe: Treat runs as the same when
app.rules.dedupe_hint: Optional expression. Two events that produce the same value inside the window become one run.
app.rules.on_error_hint: What the rest of the run does about it.
app.rules.on_error_continue: Carry on with the next action
app.rules.inbound_minted: Address made {moment}. It is shown only when it is made.
app.rules.inbound_none: No address yet: nothing can reach this rule until one is made.
app.rules.rotate_first: The address is shown once, when it is made. Put it into whatever will post to this rule, and treat it like a password — anybody who has it can start the rule.
app.rules.rotate_cost: The address in use now stops working the moment you do this. Whatever posts to it has to be given the new one.
app.rules.rotated_announced: A new address was made; the old one stops working.
app.flow.name_automatic_hint: The name is built from the rule and follows every edit. Type to give it one of your own; clear it to go back.
app.flow.sentence_trigger_inbound_webhoo: a webhook arrives at the rule's address
app.flow.card_stop_hint: the run ends here and counts as succeeded — the other arm carries on
app.flow.insert_search_hint: Type to find every step this installation serves, the ones not listed included.
app.flow.no_address: no address yet — nothing can reach this rule
app.flow.manual_hint: a button, the API, or an MCP tool
app.flow.jumble_hint: every new arrival in the inbox
app.flow.step_taken_hint: Runs inside the step: what its actions change on the entry is saved together with the step, or not at all.
app.flow.palette_hint: Click one to add it at the end, or use a + in the chain.
app.flow.inspector_nothing: Select a card on the canvas to edit it.
app.flow.blocks_only_here: Only what may go here: no trigger, and “End the run” only at the end of an arm.
app.flow.rule_tab_hint: What the rule is: its name, where it applies, whose rights it acts with, and its guardrails.
app.flow.trigger_all_six: Every trigger starts the same flow. What the trigger decides is only when a run begins.
app.flow.changed_fields: Only when one of these changed
app.flow.changed_fields_hint: None means: on every change, a rename included.
app.flow.rrule_hint: An RFC 5545 rule, such as FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO. It counts from the moment the rule was written.
app.flow.relative_offset_hint: A signed ISO 8601 duration: -PT24H is 24 hours before, P3D three days after.
app.flow.relative_hint: When the due date moves, the run moves with it. A cleared due date owes nothing, and what was due before the rule was switched on is not caught up.
app.flow.start_only_manual: Only a rule whose trigger is “{trigger}” starts by hand. Choose that trigger to start it here.
app.flow.start_needs_on: Switch the rule on to start it.
app.flow.manual_started: A run was queued. It runs as the rule's account and records that you started it.
app.flow.run_as_hint: The rule acts with this account's rights and can never exceed them, so it needs a role where the rule applies. A service account is what this usually should be: it does not leave when a person does.
app.flow.gate_hint: One condition, and it can say anything the gate can ask: a sentence, or sentences under all of, any of and none of, nested as deep as you like. None means the rule runs on every match. It is compiled when you save, so a mistake is caught here rather than at three in the morning.
app.flow.gate_before_writes: The gate sits before every write: what does not pass is recorded as skipped — the ordinary answer of a rule that is working.
app.flow.composer_expert_hint: Compiled when you save; a mistake comes back with a line and a column. Available: event, item, parent, collection, hub, actor, now, payload.
app.flow.composer_foreign: This expression was not written by the composer. Edit it as an expression, or replace it.
app.flow.card_else_if_hint: Reached when no rung above held: what the else arm held is the last resort under it.
app.flow.branch_hint: Both arms are checked when you save, and the run log names every step by its path.
app.flow.stop_hint: Ends the run here. Everything after it is marked skipped, and the run counts as succeeded — stopping early is what the rule said to do.
app.flow.wait_hint: Nothing is held open while it waits: the run is parked and resumed later.
app.flow.action_run_supplies: What the rule leaves out, the run supplies — the entry an event is about, for one.
app.flow.action_run_supplies_named: The run supplies {fields} — the rule need not.
app.flow.field_json_hint: A document whose shape the action decides.
app.flow.field_pick_none: Nothing to choose from in this scope
app.flow.field_secret_kept: Sending *** back keeps the stored secret.
app.flow.guardrails_hint: After five failed runs in a row the rule switches itself off and tells you — you, not the account it runs as.
app.flow.describe_hint: In a sentence, for example: when a request arrives, give it to Lisa.
app.flow.describe_note: The draft uses only what this workspace offers and only people, collections and labels you name. It is drawn on the canvas, switched off, and nothing runs until you switch it on.
app.flow.drafted_explains: Check it on the canvas and try it with the probe. Saving keeps it switched off.
app.flow.drafted_announced: A suggested rule is on the canvas.
app.flow.saved_off_announced: The rule was saved, switched off. Read it back before letting it loose.
app.flow.delete_body: Its runs stay in the log. This cannot be undone.
app.flow.save_first: Save the rule before switching it on.
app.flow.needs_account: Choose the account the rule runs as.
app.flow.drag_trigger: A trigger goes at the top: let it go on the trigger card, and it replaces the one there.
app.flow.drag_condition: A condition goes into the gate: let it go on “Only when”.
app.flow.drag_action: A step goes into the chain: let it go on an “Insert here”.
app.flow.drag_step: Let the card go on an “Insert here” to move it. It cannot go into its own branch.
app.flow.refused_trigger: A trigger can only be at the top. Let it go on the trigger card.
app.flow.refused_condition: A condition goes into the gate “Only when”, not into the chain.
app.flow.refused_action: A step goes on an “Insert here” between two cards.
app.flow.refused_step: A card can only go on an “Insert here”, and not into its own branch.
app.flow.refused_stop: “End the run” goes at the end of an arm, once. Let it go on the last “Insert here” of an arm — the chain ends the run anyway.
app.flow.drag_stop: “End the run” ends the run: let it go on the last “Insert here” of an arm.
app.flow.card_never_reached: Never reached: the run has ended above on every path
app.flow.refused_after_end: Nothing comes after this: the run ends above on every path.
app.flow.sheet_size: Drag to size this sheet, or use the arrow keys; pull it down to close it
app.flow.probe_intro: A sample event is dropped in at the top and travels through the rule as it stands on the canvas — unsaved changes included. Nothing is written.
app.flow.review_none: Nothing is missing: this rule can run.
app.flow.review_event_missing: This rule starts on an event and none is chosen.
app.flow.review_schedule_missing: A schedule needs a repetition rule, or it never comes round.
app.flow.review_timezone_missing: Without a time zone the schedule keeps the installation’s, which may not be yours.
app.flow.review_offset_missing: A relative date needs how far from the anchor it stands, such as P1D.
app.flow.review_step_missing: A rule on a step needs the workflow and the step.
app.flow.review_address_missing: An inbound rule is reached through an address, and none has been minted yet.
app.flow.review_runner_missing: Nobody acts yet: choose the account this rule runs as.
app.flow.review_no_steps: The rule does nothing yet: add a block to the chain.
app.flow.review_condition_empty: This condition is empty, so it says nothing about what passes.
app.flow.review_branch_condition_empty: This branch asks nothing, so every run takes the same arm.
app.flow.review_branch_empty: Both arms of this branch are empty, so it changes nothing either way.
app.flow.review_needs_entry: {kind} acts on an entry, and a scheduled run is about no entry.
app.flow.probe_event_mismatch: This sample is not the event the rule starts on, so the run will stop at the trigger.
app.flow.probe_subject_needed: A condition of this rule reads the entry, and this sample is about none: choose one above, or the condition is recorded as unreadable.
app.flow.probe_subject_hint: A real entry, found by its title. A condition that reads the entry reads this one.
app.flow.probe_payload_hint: What an inbound webhook would have carried, as JSON — what `payload` reads in a condition.
app.flow.probe_announced: The probe has run; the result is on the canvas.
app.flow.outcome_skipped: A condition did not hold — the ordinary answer of a rule that is working.
app.flow.runs_intro: What this rule has done, from its last runs. Every run is recorded, including the ones that did nothing.
app.flow.runs_draw: Draw this run on the canvas
app.flow.runs_legend: green succeeded · grey did not apply · amber held back · red failed
app.flow.health_unknown_why: Nothing to say until it has run
app.flow.check_banner_title: The check found {count} rules that need your attention.
app.flow.check_banner_one: The check found one rule that needs your attention.
app.flow.check_banner_body: {broken} cannot run and have been switched off; {attention} run, but a step would find nothing where it points. The check runs when this screen opens and when something a rule names is deleted.
app.flow.check_running: Checking the rules against what exists now
app.flow.enable_refused_broken: The check found this rule cannot run. Repair the step it names, then switch it on.
app.runs.window_reversed: The window ends before it starts.
app.flow.action.convert_jumble_entry: Turn an inbox entry into work
app.rules.inbound_minted_hint: Shown once. Post to it to start the rule, and treat it like a password — anybody who has it can start the rule.
app.rules.failing: {count} runs failed in a row. A few more and this rule switches itself off.
app.consent.title: Allow this app?
app.consent.no_request: No app is asking for anything here. Open the link the app sent you again — a consent link works once.
app.consent.asks: {app} would like to act in this workspace as you.
app.consent.unnamed_app: An app is asking to act in this workspace as you, and this installation cannot say which. Do not allow it unless you started this yourself.
app.consent.what_it_gets: What it would be able to do
app.consent.never_more: Never more than you can do yourself. If you lose a role, the app loses it at the same moment.
app.consent.withdraw_later: You can withdraw this at any time under your profile. The app stops working on its next request.
app.consent.scope.accounts_read: See who is in this workspace and what they are called
app.consent.scope.accounts_write: Invite people and change their details
app.consent.scope.admin_provisioning: Provision, find, move, suspend and end workspaces on this installation
app.consent.scope.admin_tenants: Administer every workspace on this installation
app.consent.scope.agent_destructive: Carry out actions that cannot be undone
app.consent.scope.ai_manage: Change how this workspace uses AI
app.consent.scope.backup_manage: Change where and when backups are made
app.consent.scope.backup_read: See the backups and where they go
app.consent.scope.containers_write: Create and change hubs and collections
app.consent.scope.identity_provider_mana: Change how this workspace signs people in
app.consent.scope.ops_read: See whether this installation is working
app.consent.scope.retention_manage: Change how long things are kept
app.consent.scope.retention_read: See how long things are kept
app.consent.scope.trash_read: See what is in the bin
app.consent.scope.workspace_manage: Change how this workspace is set up
app.consent.scope.workspace_read: See how this workspace is set up
app.consent.scope.config_plan: Plan changes to this workspace's configuration
app.consent.scope.config_apply: Apply changes to this workspace's configuration
app.tokens.title: Access tokens
app.tokens.intro: A token lets a script or a tool act as you, bounded by what you may do and by the scopes you give it. Nobody else can see this list, not even an administrator.
app.tokens.none_service: This service account has no tokens.
app.tokens.name: What it is for
app.tokens.name_hint: What you will read in a year when deciding whether it is still needed.
app.tokens.scopes_hint: Tick only what this token needs. Each one is a door you are opening; an unticked scope is a door that stays shut whatever the token is used for.
app.tokens.scopes_unknown: This installation has not said which scopes it offers.
app.tokens.pick_a_scope: Tick at least one scope. A token with none can do nothing.
app.tokens.name_needed: Name what the token is for, so you know it again when you revoke it.
app.tokens.expiry_needed: Choose when the token ends. There is no default.
app.tokens.expires_hint: Required, and at most a year away. There is no default on purpose: a short one gets worked around, a long one is the forever-credential this rule exists to prevent.
app.tokens.mint_above_own: This service account holds a role above yours, so only someone who holds that role can make a token for it.
app.tokens.minted_hint: Shown once. Nothing can show it again — what is kept is a hash, and no calculation turns that back into this. If you lose it, withdraw it and make another.
app.tokens.caldav_note: This is also what a calendar app asks for: with a CalDAV address from a calendar subscription, it is the password, and your address is the user name.
app.tokens.keep_first: Save the token first. It cannot be shown again.
app.tokens.minted_announced: Token minted; it is shown once.
app.tokens.installation: What may this token do on the installation?
app.tokens.installation_none_hint: No access to running the installation.
app.tokens.installation_provisioning_hin: Create and find workspaces, change their plan, suspend them, request their deletion, read limits, use and events. Recommended for a purchase platform.
app.tokens.installation_all_hint: Also the installation's settings, operators, sign-in providers and keys.
app.people.nobody_here: Nobody holds a role here yet.
app.people.granted_elsewhere: This role was granted further up. Change it where it was granted.
app.people.last_owner: The workspace needs an owner. Give somebody else Owner first.
app.people.revoke_body: {who} loses the {role} role at {where}, and what it reached is out of their reach at once. A role can be granted again afterwards.
app.people.revoke_own: You keep what is granted to you elsewhere and lose what this role reached at {where}.
app.people.revoke_own_last: It is also your last one at {where}. Afterwards nothing here is in your reach – not this screen either – until somebody grants you a role again.
app.people.responsible_hint: One person. The entry is theirs, and the last name written is the one that stands.
app.people.also_on_it_hint: Several people. They follow the entry and find it under theirs, and they are added and removed one at a time.
app.people.no_candidates: Nobody here can be named yet. Give somebody a role on this hub first.
app.people.no_match: No one matches that. Try part of a name.
app.person_picker.nobody: There is nobody here you can choose.
app.people.deciding: Working out what this type carries
app.people.auto_assign_none: The {strategy} policy ran and found nobody eligible.
app.people.auto_assign_unset: No policy chooses for this collection yet. One is set in the collection’s policies.
app.people.invite_link_announced: Invitation link created. It is shown once, below the list.
app.people.renew_link_announced: New invitation link created. The earlier one no longer works.
app.people.managed_hint: For a child, a grandparent or anybody without their own mail address: they sign in with a sign-in name and a start password Hubtask makes, and choose their own password at once.
app.people.managed_name_hint: 3 to 32 characters, no @ and no spaces. Unique in this workspace.
app.people.managed_display_hint: What everybody here sees beside this person's work.
app.people.managed_created_announced: Account added. Its start password is shown once.
app.people.managed_start_password_hint: Shown this once - Hubtask keeps no copy. Copy or print it and hand it over; it works for the first sign-in, where the person chooses their own password.
app.people.managed_kept: I have copied or printed it
app.people.managed_keep_first: Copy or print the start password first: it cannot be shown again.
app.people.managed_slip_next: Sign in with these, then choose your own password. The start password works only until then.
app.people.renew_body: For when {who} forgot their password. Their current password stops working and every device they are signed in on is signed out. A second factor they set up is still asked for. You prove it is you first.
app.people.renewed_announced: New start password for {who}. It is shown once.
app.people.address_hint_other: A link goes to this address. Once somebody with that mailbox follows it, {who} also signs in with it and can reset a forgotten password by mail - and no longer gets start passwords from you.
app.people.address_hint_own: A link goes to this address. Once you follow it, you also sign in with it and can reset a forgotten password by mail. Your sign-in name keeps working.
app.people.address_sent: A link went to {email}. It works for a day.
app.people.address_needs_password: People without an address cannot add one here: this workspace does not sign in with a password, and with an address they would sign in only through its provider, which may not know them.
app.privacy.title: People's requests
app.privacy.intro: A right somebody exercised is a case with a deadline. This is where it is recorded, carried and closed.
app.privacy.arrived: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing more arrived.} one {# more case is listed.} other {# more cases are listed.}}
app.privacy.show_closed: Show the ones that are finished
app.privacy.hide_closed: Hide the ones that are finished
app.privacy.installation_note: A request that has to reach every workspace of this installation crosses a boundary one workspace cannot. Raise it with whoever runs this installation; here you answer for this workspace.
app.privacy.extended_complexity: Extended once because the request is complex. They were told on {informed}.
app.privacy.extended_number_of_requests: Extended once because of the number of requests. They were told on {informed}.
app.privacy.archive_at: The copy was written to {target}, at {path}. There is no download here: it lies where this browser holds no credential.
app.privacy.kind_access_note: They may see what this workspace holds about them. Starting it writes a copy to a backup target.
app.privacy.kind_portability: Their data in a portable form
app.privacy.kind_portability_note: The same copy, in a shape another system can read. Starting it writes it to a backup target.
app.privacy.kind_rectification_note: Correcting something is an ordinary edit and needs no special path. It is tracked because the deadline is somebody's responsibility either way.
app.privacy.kind_restriction_note: Their record stays readable and stops being processed. Set it below, under the two with their own path.
app.privacy.kind_objection_note: The optional processing stops and everything else keeps working. Record the withdrawal below.
app.privacy.kind_erasure_note: How much is removed is your choice, and it affects other people's work. Choose it on the case before it starts.
app.privacy.mode_anonymize: Keep what other people depend on
app.privacy.mode_anonymize_note: Their name goes and their authorship becomes a former user. Tasks, comments and threads other people rely on stay where they are. This is what a case that names nothing gets, because the people who are not asking have rights too.
app.privacy.mode_full_delete_note: Everything they wrote goes with them — comments in other people's threads, tasks other people were working from. Choose this only when you owe it: what other people depended on does not come back.
app.privacy.start_makes_archive: Starting this writes the copy. It goes to the backup target the case names.
app.privacy.reject_reason_hint: Required. A refusal without a reason is not an answer.
app.privacy.extend_note: A deadline can be extended once, when the request is complex or there are many. Tell the person first, and why: this records that you did, it does not write to them.
app.privacy.extend_informed_hint: Required. Not before the request arrived, and not after today.
app.privacy.record_note: Recording opens the case and starts its clock. Nothing is collected, exported or removed until you start answering it.
app.privacy.subject_email_hint: For somebody with no account here. One of the two is enough.
app.privacy.subject_account_hint: The person the case is about, where they have an account here.
app.privacy.subject_needed: Name the person by an address or an account.
app.privacy.target_hint: A copy of somebody's data has to be put somewhere, and this installation writes archives to configured targets.
app.privacy.received_on_hint: The day the request reached you. Leave it empty if that was today.
app.privacy.deadline_hint: Optional. Without one the case is owed one calendar month from the day of receipt. With one, it is owed until the end of that day.
app.privacy.articles_title: The two with their own path
app.privacy.register_title: Who keeps their content out of AI
app.privacy.register_note: Their entries, comments and notes go into no prompt, and their name is left out of what does. Only this screen lists them.
app.privacy.register_empty: Nobody keeps their content out of AI.
app.privacy.articles_note: Restricting processing and withdrawing a consent are not cases: they are states you set, and each is recorded.
app.privacy.restrict_note: Their record stays readable and stays where it is. What stops is processing: no automation acts on it and nothing is asked of a model about it. Their sessions keep working — this is not a lock on the person.
app.privacy.withdraw_note: The optional processing stops and everything else keeps working. The withdrawal is recorded rather than erased: what was lawful when is what somebody will ask about.
app.privacy.purpose_hint: What this installation offers, for example ai_processing.
app.privacy.withdraw_account_hint: Leave it empty for your own.
app.privacy.confirm_erase_anonymize: {name}'s name, address, password and every token and device go, and their authorship becomes a former user. What they wrote stays where other people rely on it. This cannot be undone.
app.privacy.confirm_erase_full_delete: {name}'s account goes, and every comment they wrote goes with it. The entries they created stay, credited to nobody. This cannot be undone.
app.privacy.preview_checking: Checking what the legal holds would keep…
app.privacy.preview_unknown: Whether a legal hold would keep part of this could not be checked. The erasure still keeps whatever a hold covers.
app.privacy.preview_none: No legal hold reaches this person: everything the mode names goes.
app.privacy.preview_intro: Legal holds keep part of this. It is kept and restricted rather than erased - for legal claims, Art. 17(3)(e) GDPR - and the rest of the erasure runs when each hold is lifted:
app.privacy.kept_part: A hold on {scope} keeps {comments, plural, =0 {no comment} one {# comment} other {# comments}}, {assignments, plural, =0 {no assignment} one {# assignment} other {# assignments}} and their name on {entries, plural, =0 {no entry} one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
app.privacy.kept_part_account: A hold on {scope} keeps the account itself, restricted, with {comments, plural, =0 {no comment} one {# comment} other {# comments}}, {assignments, plural, =0 {no assignment} one {# assignment} other {# assignments}} and {entries, plural, =0 {no entry} one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
app.privacy.kept_partly: Partly completed: {holds, plural, one {a legal hold keeps} other {# legal holds keep}} part of it, for legal claims (Art. 17(3)(e) GDPR). The rest is erased when the hold is lifted.
app.privacy.kept_waits: Partly completed. The rest waits: the person still runs {rules, plural, one {# automation rule} other {# automation rules}}. Point them at another account or remove them.
app.privacy.kept_waits_owner: Partly completed. The rest waits: the person is this workspace's only owner. Give somebody else Owner first.
app.privacy.kept_rest_erased: The rest was erased on {at}, once no legal hold kept it.
app.activity.label: What happened to this entry
app.activity.none: Nothing has happened to this entry yet.
app.audit.title: The trail
app.audit.intro: Every action this workspace records about itself. What it holds is who, what and when — never what anybody wrote.
app.audit.none: Nothing in the trail matches that.
app.audit.arrived: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing more arrived.} one {# more entry arrived.} other {# more entries arrived.}}
app.audit.end: That is every entry for this query.
app.audit.action_hint: The start of an action name is enough — “auth.” finds every sign-in event.
app.audit.actor_hint: Without the right to the whole trail, only your own events are answered.
app.audit.reading_is_not_recorded: Reading the trail is not itself recorded — a trail that grew by being read would bury what it is for. A refusal is recorded, and so is an export.
app.audit.actor_gone: Somebody who is no longer in this workspace
app.audit.changed_sensitive: {field} changed — the trail keeps that it changed, not what it became
app.audit.verify_intro: Every entry is chained to the one before it. Checking the chain over a period says whether anything has been altered or removed since.
app.audit.never_anchored: This proves the chain is intact inside the database. Nothing has anchored it outside one yet, so it says nothing against somebody who could rewrite all of it.
app.audit.verify_anchors: Also read the last anchor back
app.audit.verify_anchors_hint: Fetches the last anchor from the backup target and compares the chain end it holds with the chain here. A read of another machine, so it is asked for rather than always done.
app.audit.anchor_read: The copy at the target, taken {at}, seals the chain up to entry {seq}, and the chain here computes to the same end.
app.audit.anchor_disagrees_explains: The chain end kept outside this database is not the one this database computes at that entry. Whatever the walk inside said, the chain below the anchor is not what it was when it was sealed.
app.audit.anchor_unreadable: The anchor could not be read back
app.audit.anchoring_intro: Once a day, the chain's end — the last entry's number and its hash — is written as a small file to a backup target of this workspace. That copy is what says something against somebody who could rewrite the whole database.
app.audit.anchoring_off: Not anchored. The chain proves tampering inside the database only.
app.audit.anchoring_target_hint: Choose a target with object lock and a retention no shorter than the audit period: an anchor that expires before the entries it seals is a seal nobody can check. The files are a few hundred bytes each, so the lock can be long.
app.audit.anchoring_choose_first: Choose a target the chain is not anchored to yet.
app.audit.anchoring_on_announced: Anchoring switched on; the first anchor is written after the next midnight.
app.audit.anchoring_off_announced: Anchoring switched off; the anchors already written stay.

app.voice.title: Voice assistants
app.voice.intro: Put things on lists by voice: "Alexa, ask Hubtask: butter on the shopping list." Every entry is made as the person who linked their account, with exactly their rights.
app.voice.enabled_hint: Off: Alexa says that voice entries are switched off for this workspace.
app.voice.default_list_hint: Where a thing goes when no list is said: "Alexa, ask Hubtask: butter".
app.voice.names_hint: Every collection and every category is understood by its own name, "shopping list" for "Shopping" included. Add a name here where people say something else, such as "fridge" for the shopping list or "Metro" for a category.
app.voice.try_hint: Type what someone would say after "Alexa, ask Hubtask". Nothing is added.
app.voice.try_example: stock cubes and two litres of milk at Costco
app.voice.result_default: {things} would go on the default list, {list}.
app.voice.result_ambiguous: Several lists sound like that: {lists}. Alexa would ask which one.
app.voice.result_none: {things} has no list: name one, or choose a default list.
app.voice.installation_skill: This installation publishes a Hubtask skill. Enable it in the Alexa app, link your Hubtask account there, and say "Alexa, open Hubtask".
app.voice.alexa_hint: Your own skill, free in Amazon's Alexa developer console. It stays in development and works on every Echo of your Amazon account. Amazon calls this installation over HTTPS, so it has to be reachable from the internet with a valid certificate - through a reverse proxy or a tunnel where it runs at home.
app.voice.step_skill_hint: In developer.amazon.com/alexa/console/ask: Create skill, name it Hubtask, choose your language, the Custom model and "Provision your own". You choose the invocation name here; it is also in the model you paste in the next step.
app.voice.step_model_hint: Copy the model and paste it under Interaction Model → JSON Editor, then Save and Build. Once is enough: your lists are not in the model, Hubtask teaches them to Alexa with every answer - new and renamed lists work at once.
app.voice.step_endpoint_hint: Under Endpoint choose HTTPS, enter this address and "My development endpoint has a certificate from a trusted certificate authority".
app.voice.step_linking_hint: Under Account Linking switch it on, choose "Auth Code Grant" and tick PKCE (SHA-256) - without it Alexa sends no PKCE proof and signing in ends without a link. Paste the vendor ID from the Alexa Redirect URLs there (the last part of each address) and make the linking here; then copy each value into the console.
app.voice.vendor_id_hint: The end of an Alexa Redirect URL: …/api/skill/link/<vendor ID>
app.voice.linking_made: The linking is made. Copy the client ID and secret now.
app.voice.client_secret_hint: Shown this once. Paste it into the console now.
app.voice.step_skill_id_hint: At the top of the skill in the console: Copy Skill ID. Hubtask answers only this skill.
app.voice.step_test_hint: In the Alexa app: More → Skills & Games → Your Skills → Dev → Hubtask → Enable, and sign in with the Hubtask account. Then always use the invocation name: "Alexa, ask {name}: stock cubes at Costco" or "Alexa, open {name}". Without it a sentence goes to Amazon's own list.
app.voice.scope_hint: Enter each scope on its own with "+ Add scope".
app.consent.incomplete: An app is asking here, but its request lacks something Hubtask requires. It is set in the app that offers the link:
app.consent.missing_code_challenge: The PKCE proof (code_challenge). For Alexa: switch PKCE with SHA-256 on under Account Linking in the developer console.
app.consent.missing_scope: The permissions (scope). For Alexa: enter the scopes from Administration → Voice assistants under Account Linking.
app.voice.invocation_hint: What follows "Alexa, open …": two words at least, written apart the way Alexa writes them (German joins two nouns into one; an adjective with a noun stays apart). Not allowed: "Alexa", "Echo", "skill", "app", launch words such as "open" or "ask", and connecting words such as "to", "with" or "for". Leave empty for the default.
voice.invocation_invalid: An invocation name has two words at least and at most 50 characters, starts with a letter and holds only letters and spaces. Not allowed: "Alexa", "Echo", "skill", "app", launch words such as "open" or "ask", connecting words such as "to", "with" or "for", and an article as the second word.
